column1: # Cells whose answer here is not PostgreSQL 17.11's, for count_distinct_recombined_arms_test.go (#1696). Every line is a residual,
# wrong at the base f0b84410 too (TestCountDistinctRecombinedDump at the base, compared cell by cell), and every line answers exactly
# what the base answers, value and declared type, except two: cteDupName sumInt/ungrouped on the single-process arms keeps the base's
# wrong VALUE (the first column read twice) and now declares PostgreSQL's bigint where the base declared numeric.
# name<TAB>arms (all | dag | single: the two single-process arms)<TAB>this engine's answer<TAB>why-code.
# A kept line whose arm starts answering PostgreSQL FAILS: re-measure and delete it. The why-codes:
#   scale: display scale (per-value scale program): AVG answers fewer fraction digits than PostgreSQL's numeric

#   scalarScaleErr: a scalar subquery over a rewritten AVG(int) is refused on every arm (numeric field overflow: 23.333333 does not fit a DECIMAL at scale 4). The subquery's column is declared from its UNOPTIMIZED plan (physical subqueryLogicalPlan, no two-level rewrite: AVG(int) DECIMAL(38,4)) while the executed plan is optimized (the rewrite's division, scale 6)
#   union346: (#346) a UNION ALL arm that selects an aggregate is refused by the DAG planner; on an `all` line the single-process arms are refused for sharedNameFinal's reason

#   cteDupName: a CTE column-alias list over a body that publishes one name twice reads the FIRST column for both on the single-process path (logical applyColumnAliasProject renames by name); with or without the rewrite (the grouped cells), and on the DAG arms where the plan routes to that path

#   unionArmType: a UNION ALL of grouped arms whose outputs share a name declares MIN/MAX of an integer bigint where PostgreSQL declares integer, on the single-process arms; the rewrite declines these (grouped, not lone)

#   sharedNameFinal: (#1692's shared-name line) two outputs share a name and the rewrite builds its finalizing projection (an ungrouped COUNT or an AVG beside the COUNT(DISTINCT)); that projection reads level 2 by NAME. On the single-process arms it reads the first same-named column for both: refused where the second output's declaration disagrees with that column (#361 store guard), answered twice otherwise. On the DAG the stage planner declines the projection (aggregatePublishesADuplicateName) and the plan goes on without it: a dropped COALESCE answers NULL for a zero-row COUNT. The recombined aggregates there keep the base's numeric declaration, so that the guard's refusal is not turned into the first value answered twice
